Updated request scope as of 5/17/24 refinement sent by Mr.Small:

We have put some thought into search restrictions and terms and here is what we would suggest:

(1) total time range of January 1, 2023 through July 31, 2023
(2) Anything that includes Juli Beth Hinds, Dr. Amy Lerner, urban studies and planning (USP), global policy & strategy (GPS), UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms
(3) Anything related to the regional water equity report or RDF
(4) Anything containing a reference to "Juli Beth Hinds, Dr Amy Lerner,  Geosyntec, USP, GPS, or the RWER or RDF", UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms sent to or from "Elise Ruiz, anyone at Murakawa Communications, anyone at Geosyntec including but not limited to Ken Susillo, Megan Otto, Stephanie Zinn; and anyone at the County including but not limited to Stephanie Gaines, Crystal Benham, Todd Snyder, Sarah Agassi, Eden Brukman, and Murtaza Baxamusa"

Original Request:

To Whom it may Concern:
I am writing on behalf of my client Juli Beth Hinds. On behalf of Ms. Hinds, please consider this a formal request pursuant to California Public Records Act, Government Code §6250 et seq. for copies of all DOCUMENTS of the County of San Diego Land Use & Environment Group that reference or relate to: Juli Beth Hinds; the Department of Urban Studies and Planning at the University of California San Diego; or Nathan Fletcher. ("DOCUMENTS" as used herein, shall be defined to mean any ''writing'' as that term is defined in Evidence Code section 250, including, but not limited to, correspondence, emails, texts, communications of any kind, recordings, tapes, computer print-outs, records, slides, photographs, notes, working papers, written analyses, memoranda, plans, telegraphs, telexes and transcriptions, electronic data, and notes or memoranda made by any telephone communications.) This request encompasses all DOCUMENTS dated or created between the dates of January 1, 2022 through the date of this letter.
I request delivery of these records to our firm's office, located at 402 W. Broadway, Suite 1270, San Diego, CA 92101, or we can arrange to pick them up at a reasonable location designated by the County.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Subject: FW: Climate Action Research Grant - Letter of Intent (LOI) Due Jan 17th

Sarah-

My team met with the group described below on Friday (UCSD, SANDAG, Climate Action Campaign was added & UCSD spoke with the City of SD earlier so they did not join).  UCSD is looking for us to sign onto a Letter of Intent by COB today including providing bios and resumes of key staff.  The LOI is a precursor to be able to apply for the grant.   In short, there is much to be flushed out with this research effort before committing to join a grant application.  We don’t think there is application to the CAP but there may be for the Sustainable Land Use Framework, possibly RDF and other data analyses that the PODS could lead.  It is not clear if the ROI would be there for us.  This type of thing can easily balloon into a substantial work effort, which we would not be able to commit to with our current project responsibilities.  However, the City plans to join (I believe SANDAG does, too, but confirming) and we think it would be better to sign on than miss the opportunity, recognizing that the LOI is an initial formality and we can drop off prior to grant application if we determine the ROI doesn’t pencil.  We were very transparent with the group that it sounds like there are exciting possibilities here but we cannot commit until we know more.

Question by COB: Are you ok with us moving forward at this preliminary stage, recognizing we will need to flush out more details and reassess prior to joining on any formal application? (We can also give the BOS offices a heads up asap, if so.)

Hi Murtaza and all -  great meeting on Friday and we received a lot of DCAO input and direction. I added the main action items below, based on Sarah’s feedback.

  1.  Regional Decarbonization Framework
     *   DCAO: we need to foster the business community as well as workforce. Wherever we talk about green jobs we need to talk about green industry. They go hand in hand.
                                                               i.      Murtaza need to follow up with David Flores - the items on green industry that Sarah shared was not included in Chairwoman's talking points
                                                             ii.      We need to highlight both -- it is not one or the other -- Sarah needs help reinforcing this piece with D1 (or else we will face obstacles in the business community.

     *   DCAO feedback on Symposium: Donna needs to be engaged on this -- she needs to take the lead on this. Sarah requests a meeting (30 min) to talk about the symposium
                                                               i.      We need to come back with Sarah on our plan to move forward, then have another call with David and other partners

     *   DCAO feedback on D3 convening: need to put a timeframe of when the convening needs to take place. If she can't make it then we need to move forward on it. Hold them to a timeline (because we need it for the BL, Board hearing, etc.). Can't have their district missing in this.
     *   DCAO question for us to consider: Because we are bringing this home through public health -- for purposes of when we go to the Board - should we tee up some joint Public Health approach/PPT for March hearing?
     *   DCAO: how many Playbook copies are we printing? Maybe print one for each Board office and our office -- like 30 or 40
     *   DCAO: Sarah wants information as the comments come in on the Playbook -- we may not include things proactively -- but have them discuss in the public setting
  1.  Regional Equity Group
     *   For when Murakawa meets with Sarah: how do we ensure all of our communities are represented? Not just cities, but unincorporated as well. Who will they engage? Who are the players for the
                                                               i.      What info do we need to provide them so they are educated about San Diego region dynamics -- this will be important
                                                             ii.      Connect Murakawa with PDS EJ team

  1.  Regional Water Equity Project
     *   DCAO: always Board office that moves a Board letter forward - they should be in the know. But also the whole Board took action. Start with key Board office, and then say that we are going to share with all office because we need to meet the needs. Different Board offices will have different perspectives of this -- like all the ag and Borrego Springs (worst groundwater impacted in the State) -- they have critical needs.
                                                               i.      For the one pager -- who needs to weigh in, in additional to the Board offices -- Donna, Michael. Need people far removed to review and provide insight

     *   DCAO: would like a timeline on all aspects of outreach, when will we start to make the pitch - before it starts
  1.  Misc.
     *   DCAO briefing request: would like a briefing on Spring Valley communities in terms of what we are doing for TCC grant.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Ron Nehring, Crest Planning Group Chairman <
ronnehring@ronnehring.ccsend.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 27, 2025 at 3:26 PM
Subject: PLANNING GROUP: What we have done so far on wildfire
To: <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com>

Fellow Planning Group Chairs,

Following the interest and feedback I received regarding our new Firewise
USA site, I wanted to share additional resources and insights from our work
on wildfire preparedness and evacuation in our subregion. I’m also
interested in knowing what work your Planning Group has done that perhaps
we have not thought of so we can strengthen our efforts.

In 2021, our Planning Group established a dedicated working group on
wildfire and evacuation. Over the course of three years, we held meetings
and engaged extensively with stakeholders—including our local fire
district, Cal Fire, the Crest Fire Safe Council, representatives from the
County, the Sheriff’s Department, and others—to identify the most effective
ways to reduce wildfire risk and enhance evacuation capacity.

This effort culminated in a comprehensive package of seven wildfire-related
resolutions, which our Planning Group unanimously adopted in the summer of
2024. Given our advisory role to the County of San Diego, each resolution
is framed as a recommendation to County. You can review the full package of
resolutions, along with a summary, here: Crest Planning Group Fire
Resolutions.
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJVShatP__5WDqsOxEzOSLt0N1DkC0uglT12fnpaypLueU2s1G3PpLX2QIxvykqsJlEMDcC2miEM8Bqv622WJ-69pcxx7i8NhOTmgjqk0B0mJfPKWnaIxBjT80ovcsz0UKyYqnOwPhYVdrhyFb7VvbHFgfL3SukQfI6qrOJzATK-R_tAmMvo4ITcM4-w9Z2LD4LLQyr3L6ijIc_JBgR4xPXZ5jMCN4IXalwne9xF64Dap01AmRYnkT7NxXK9j5oEi_w==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>

One key takeaway from our work was the value of the Firewise USA program
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyDxoyackA2RcQNTEfRlDPkbHmX2MuO8PBPswQ8KgE-rcyjYWxx1MCWnw0BK9QNwVPRmMPe--vv-_HOnhwjgONujomYHLomm1G-istWt-z54Z9ytb_uSjY54cNszAN2-4h6nrYtrH8BE9W20iK5zGCgg==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>,
which allows groups of at least eight homeowners to establish a Firewise
USA site, take steps to reduce wildfire risk, and potentially qualify for
homeowners insurance discounts.

Recognizing its benefits, one of our seven resolutions specifically
encourages and supports the formation of Firewise USA sites throughout our
subregion.

After I became Chairman of our Planning Group, we launched a website to
better serve our residents by providing access to essential information.
While the County’s webpage for our Planning Group exists, it is difficult
to find and lacks comprehensive resources. Our goal was to create a one-stop
hub where residents can find details about our Planning Group’s work,
wildfire preparedness, code enforcement, defensible space requirements, and
more. You can visit the site at: CrestPlanningGroup.com
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyNiKG57PrvAcVhxPjLGUulw37A996ASKMyLn1vsnrei-gZWKYuy2livonBtHIF9k9VG_wnP-b7EVEi0hg9ftQc50vEBE2M1Z12ueCdNq6VOI=&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>
.

At our next Planning Group meeting on Monday, February 10 at 6:30 PM at the
Crest Community Association Clubhouse, 113 North Park Drive, El Cajon we
will discuss the Firewise USA program and how to establish additional sites
in our subregion. I invite you to join us for this discussion—if you or

emails.subject: Introducing Street Stewards - A grassroots initiative to keep San Diego’s street clean one block at a time!
emails.body:
Dear East County Community Groups,

I am writing to inform you of a powerful new mapping tool developed specifically for San Diegans to help keep our streets clean together. My non-profit organization is called Street Stewards, and we are nearly 1,000 volunteers strong… and counting! We have developed a website where any San Diego County citizen can log in, find their local community, and adopt a block by recording litter pickups on our live interactive map.

Our powerful interactive map shows the health of the entire county’s streets with a color coded system which enables Stewards to decide to simply clean their own block OR go to where their efforts are needed most. Please see the attached graphics for an overview of how it works and an example of how our interactive map appears.

This website was developed with generous help from San Diego County’s Neighborhood Reinvestment Program grants, and it is a free tool for anyone to use! We would love your help in spreading the word about it with your membership, organization, and constituents. The strength of this model relies on participation and widespread adoption, so it is time to get the word out.

We are excited to collaborate to spread the word in your newsletters, emails, social media posts, and among your friends and colleagues! You can learn much more and sign up here: www.streetstewards.com. I am happy to provide more information, attend meetings and present, or explain further. Please don’t hesitate to get in touch with ideas about how to get the word out! Thank you for your time, and I look forward to working with you to make San Diego a more beautiful place - one block at a time.

Sincerely,

Aaron Null
Founder, Executive Director
Street Stewards
